source.title: Weak Critics Make Strong Learners: On-Policy Critique Distillation for Scalable Oversight
source.authors: Can Jin; Jiakang Li; Rui Wu; Edwin Zhang; Dimitris N. Metaxas

page_placements.theme: A weaker model's text inserted into a stronger model's inference (rewritten prompts, RL-trained instructions, critiques, short reasoning segments)

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: Applies weak-to-strong oversight in a new setting: weak models critique strong-model answers rather than label them, and the study reports inference-time and training-time outcomes. It does not test the label-based intervention or PGR specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly replaces weak labels with critiques. It reports no PGR and does not compare a strong model fine-tuned on weak labels against its weak labeler. Rows record related critique-based results only; these are not direct tests of V1–V6. The paper also reports other critique-quality baselines and training checkpoints; omissions are listed below.
record.test_reason: Not a test of any version. The weak model only critiques; it never labels, and no strong model is fine-tuned on weak labels. No PGR, weak-label baseline or strong ceiling is reported. OPCD's critique filter also checks refined answers against ground truth, so training is not weak-only supervision. The study frames itself within weak-to-strong work but measures critique-and-refine and critique distillation gains over the strong model's own baseline. That is a related construct, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Weak critiques improve frozen strong models at inference time, and critique quality is central. OPCD improves strong models during training, and reasoning training is noisier and more sensitive to critique quality than alignment training.
record.recipe_differences: Uses critiques and critique-conditioned self-teacher distillation rather than training a strong model on weak-model labels; it also includes inference-time critique-and-refine. PGR is not calculated.
record.method_sensitivity: Critique quality changes outcomes: selected high-quality critiques perform better, while low-quality critiques can reduce performance. The reported training trajectories also vary by task, with less smooth reasoning results than alignment results.

fits_no_version.finding: Weak-model critique plus strong-model refinement raises pass@k over strong-only sampling on GPQA Diamond, IFEval and AIME. IFEval pass@1 rises from 61.61 to 72.11; the GPQA pass@1 gain is small (50.51 to 51.99).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time critiques from a weaker model can improve a stronger model's accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: OPCD raises validation scores above the initial model: IFEval best mean@8 68.74 vs 61.60; GPQA best mean@8 42.67 vs 38.22. Trajectories are non-monotonic, and GPQA pass@8 drops to 66.12 at one step. The critique filter uses ground-truth outcome checks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distilling outcome-filtered weak critiques into a strong model improves validation accuracy, more stably for alignment than for reasoning.

fits_no_version.finding: Critique quality matters. Oracle-selected 'best' critiques give the highest GPQA pass@16 (92.42). 'Worst' critiques drop GPQA pass@4 to 68.18 vs 74.75 and give roughly S-only performance at pass@8 and pass@16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Misleading weak critiques can harm strong-model refinement.

record.peer_reviewed: The 3rd AI for Math Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), 2026
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the listed results. The paper's training comparisons do not isolate OPCD against a naive weak-label fine-tuning baseline, and the reported training checkpoints are not uniformly monotonic.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit required omissions. From Table 1, pass@2, pass@4, and pass@8 for the main critique-and-refine results, and additional S-only/W-only and random-critique values, are omitted. From Table 3, intermediate validation checkpoints beyond the selected steps are omitted. Table 2 alignment validation checkpoints are retained at its reported validation steps.

untested.parts: No strong model is trained on weak labels and compared with the weak supervisor; no PGR.
No confidence loss, ensembling or loss variant is compared with naive weak-label fine-tuning by PGR.
No PGR variation by size or task is measured; only one weak/strong pair per setting.
Misleading critiques are studied, but not exploitation of uncheckable errors, distribution shift or shared errors under weak-label training.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'tests'/T3 to 'discusses'/T6: no row bears on any version and the reader assigned no labels. OPCD keeps only critiques whose refined answer is correct by ground truth, so the training signal uses gold outcome information. No weak-label or ground-truth SFT baseline is run. No uncertainty is reported. AIME uses 60 problems, so a 3.3-point difference is about two problems.

versions.untested_parts: No strong student is fine-tuned on weak-model labels and compared with the weak labeler using PGR.
No auxiliary confidence loss, weak-supervisor ensembling, or loss variant is compared by PGR against naive weak-label fine-tuning.
The paper varies model pair and task for critique-based methods, but does not measure PGR or test its variation by supervisor/student size and task as specified.
It studies helpful versus misleading critiques, but not supervisor-uncheckable exploitation, distribution shift, or shared weak/strong error effects.
No theoretical conditions for a student to beat its supervisor are established.
No vision or other non-language modality is tested.

relation.reason: The paper explicitly discusses weak-to-strong generalization and proposes related oversight methods, but its results do not establish any of the catalog's specified versions.

tranche.reason: The experiments measure critique-assisted inference and critique-conditioned self-distillation, rather than strong-model training on weak labels with gains over the weak supervisor or naive weak-label fine-tuning. No listed claim version is tested.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate. Worst-critique baselines select critiques using answer correctness; OPCD training filters critiques using outcome-correctness and rubric checks, so its supervision is not weak-only.
